verdict.rationale: AWS IAM's own docs show JSON policies that control which AWS resources users can access. They cover nine policy types, including identity-based, resource-based and permissions boundaries, attachable to identities or resources, which supports resource-level scoping. Nothing in the pack documents condition keys or the policy evaluation logic, so only about half the story is evidenced. Missing for 10: evidence of condition keys/condition blocks, documented policy evaluation logic (explicit deny/allow precedence), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, least privilege is expressible — fine-grained IAM policies with conditions, resource-level scoping, and documented policy evaluation

citations.quote: With IAM, you can manage permissions that control which AWS resources users can access.
AWS supports nine types of policies: identity-based policies, resource-based policies, VPC endpoint policies, permissions boundaries
Manage access in AWS by creating policies and attaching them to IAM identities (users, groups of users, or roles) or AWS resources.
